samples.summary: `asFiniteNumber` treats numeric strings as absent, so the new bands silently zero/delete stored string numerics (listLevel "2" → 0, fontSize "24" → deleted, string image size → image dropped) and then write the loss back
samples.evidence: `bandOneBlock` gates every field on `asFiniteNumber(value)` = `typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : undefined`. For `block.listLevel = "2"` that yields `undefined`, and `normalizeListLevel(undefined)` returns 0 (list-level.ts:44, `raw ?? 0`), so the block is rewritten to level 0 — nesting lost. Likewise `inlineStyle.fontSize = "24"` is `delete`d (numeric-attrs.ts:320-322) and an image with `width:"300"` is deleted (324-332, via `asFiniteNumber(...) ?? NaN`). This is not hypothetical here: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:95-99, added by this same change, states the v1 PUT "never looks at `listLevel`, so `{\"type\":\"list-item\",\"listLevel\":\"2\"}` is stored as the *string* it was sent as" and that without a `Number(...)` coercion "such a level would flatten to 0 … silently". The same gate is now added at packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1036 (so a GET→edit→PUT round-trip persists 0) and in packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts, where `withTextElement`/`withShapeText`/`withTableCellBody`/`setNotes` band on the way in and then always write back — making the flattening permanent on the first edit. Coercing with `Number(...)` before the band (as the PPTX exporter deliberately does) would preserve the value.

samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` drops out-of-band ratios instead of substituting 0, shifting later columns left and reducing `numCols`; the two sibling bands added in the same change do the opposite
samples.evidence: `if (ratio === undefined) continue;` removes the entry entirely, so one non-finite value (`Number('1e400') === Infinity`) shortens `columnWidths`. `columnWidths.length` is `computeTableLayout`'s `numCols` (view/table-layout.ts:153), so the last column is never laid out and its cells' content disappears; re-serializing the model then persists the shortened `cols`. The two other implementations of the same rule in this change deliberately preserve position — `normalizeColumnRatio(...) ?? 0` at numeric-attrs.ts:348 and docs-content.controller.ts:1055, both commented "so every later column keeps its index". Separately, `cols === ''` now yields `[]` (0 columns) where the previous `split(',').map(Number).filter(!isNaN)` yielded `[0]` (1 column).

samples.summary: The paste sanitizer bands rowHeights, padding, fontSize and lineHeight but leaves `columnWidths` unbanded, so a pasted out-of-band ratio persists and diverges from the band every reader now applies
samples.evidence: `for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 1 / cols);` — `asNumber` only checks finiteness, so a payload ratio of `1e9` is written into the CRDT unchanged. Both CRDT read boundaries now clamp ratios to `MAX_COLUMN_RATIO` (crdt-tree.ts:222, yorkie-doc-store.ts:479), so the pasting client renders geometry no peer and no later reload reproduces — the exact producer/reader divergence the sibling edits in this same file (rowHeights at 341, padding at 268, fontSize at 165, lineHeight at 215) were added to close.
searchedFor: read clipboard.ts sanitizeTableData / sanitizeCellStyle / sanitizeBlockStyle / sanitizeCell
grep columnWidths in clipboard.ts and table-layout.ts

samples.summary: The slides PUT band covers inline `fontSize` but not the inline image size, unlike `bandBlockNumerics`, so an out-of-band image is accepted and stored and then silently dropped by every reader
samples.evidence: `normalizeSlideInlines` bands only `style.fontSize`; there is no `isPaintableImageSize` check on `style.image.width/height`. The client-side band for the same codec-free bodies does drop such an image (numeric-attrs.ts:323-332), and both CRDT readers drop it too. A PUT of `image: {width: 1e9, height: 10}` is therefore accepted, echoed back to the caller as stored, and rendered as no image at all by every viewer — and the frontend slides store writes that dropped state back on the next edit. An image height is a line height, the same sink the fontSize band on the adjacent line guards.
searchedFor: read docs-content.controller.ts assertValidSlideBlocks / normalizeSlideInlines / bandSlideBlockNumerics / bandSlideCellNumerics

samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` truncates a legitimately tall table row: the 200th fragment absorbs all remaining height and overflows its page, so the rest of the row paints off-page
samples.evidence: `if (++fragments >= MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN) fragHeight = remaining;` makes the 200th fragment take the whole remainder regardless of `pageAvail`. Row heights are also derived from real cell content (computeTableLayout steps 3–4 sum genuine line heights), so a table cell with roughly 10,000 lines legitimately exceeds 200 pages; its tail is then laid out past the page content box and clipped rather than paginated. The bound is the right shape for poisoned input but is applied unconditionally to honest input too.

samples.summary: Indent is refused for a whole subtree whenever any descendant sits at MAX_LIST_LEVEL, so Tab on an ancestor (or select-all + Tab) silently does nothing even when most items have room
samples.evidence: `if (delta > 0 && deepest >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL) continue;` refuses the entire subtree, and a selected descendant is only reconsidered if it is itself under the ceiling. For [a:0, b:1, c:8] with all three selected, a's subtree is refused, b's subtree (b,c) is refused, and c is refused — a complete no-op with no feedback though a and b had room. Documented and tested as intended, so flagged as a behaviour note rather than a defect.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `asFiniteNumber` (numeric-attrs.ts:256-258) returns `undefined` for any non-number, and the bands built on it flatten `listLevel` to 0 (numeric-attrs.ts:310-312 with list-level.ts:43-46 `raw ?? 0`), delete a string `fontSize` (numeric-attrs.ts:320-322), and delete an inline image whose width/height are strings (numeric-attrs.ts:323-332 via `?? NaN`). The same gate exists server-side (docs-content.controller.ts:1002-1004, 1035-1037, 1206-1208) on a path that repairs in place and stores/echoes the repaired payload (assertValidSlideBlocks:1113-1114), and the frontend store bands on read and then unconditionally writes back on every edit (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2253-2268, 2300-2331, 2343-2349), making the loss permanent. That string-typed numerics genuinely occur in verbatim-persisted slide bodies is documented by this same change in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:88-103, which deliberately coerces with `Number(...)`, as does the docs codec at yorkie-doc-store.ts:533. No caller or validator coerces/rejects string numerics before reaching these bands, so there is no guard making it unreachable and no basis for not-present or out-of-scope; silent value loss written back to storage is in the correctness lane.
